blocks.text: High bleeding risk; hold anticoagulants/antiplatelets per policy.

items: High bleeding risk.
Warfarin: hold 5 days and confirm INR <= 1.8.
IV unfractionated heparin: hold 4-6 hours and check aPTT or anti-Xa.
Enoxaparin: hold 1 dose if prophylactic; hold 2 doses or 24 hours if therapeutic.
DOACs: use agent- and CrCl-specific timing in the anticoagulation table.
Clopidogrel: hold 5 days.
Aspirin: hold 3-5 days.

lies along the inferior liver surface; identify the fundus, body, and neck.
connects the gallbladder neck to the extrahepatic biliary tree; neck or duct obstruction can prevent drainage.
traverses liver before entering the gallbladder; assess intervening hepatic vessels.
enters the gallbladder without traversing liver; requires a safe window without intervening bowel.

transhepatic access carries greater bleeding risk but may help contain bile leakage. Transperitoneal access avoids liver traversal but has a theoretical greater bile-leak/biloma risk; comparative studies have not consistently shown a difference in leakage. Choose the safest patient-specific route.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Regular diet.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
Pigtail drain - flush orders 10 mL daily.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: resume the day after the procedure.
IV unfractionated heparin: restart after 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: restart after 12 hours.
DOACs: Table 6 generally lists 24 hours; confirm agent, renal function, and local policy.
Clopidogrel: restart after 6 hours at 75 mg or 24 hours if using a 300-600-mg loading dose.
Aspirin: resume the day after the procedure.
